Subject: POC Observability: next steps & success criteria

Hi Sara / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about FintechX's evaluation goals. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed POC plan and the observability scope so we have aligned success criteria and owners. I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short checklist for observability.

High-level POC scope (2-week POC):
- Goal: validate that Redwood inference meets FintechX latency & cost targets for your payment workflows and that observability gives you actionable signals for production readiness.
- Environment: Redwood hosted sandbox with a pinned model variant (we'll provide details).
- Timeline: kickoff week of Mar 29, POC targets complete by Apr 12.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 350ms for sandbox traffic representative of production (50–500 tokens).
2) Reliability: error rate (5xx or failed responses) < 0.5% over POC window.
3) Cost: token spend per 1k requests within agreed threshold (we'll provide estimates).
4) Observability: dashboard with realtime panels + alerting for p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, model token counts, and cache-hit metrics.
5) Tracing/logs: sample traces integrated with your APM and structured log export to S3 (or preferred storage).

Observability deliverables (what Redwood will provide):
- Pre-built dashboard mockups (Datadog/Grafana) and a sample metrics set.
- OpenTelemetry tracing integration guide and sample spans for end-to-end request traces.
- Structured logs (JSON) export instructions and retention plan.
- Runbook for common POC alerts and recommended thresholds.

Owners / asks (please confirm):
- Redwood: Marcus (dashboards/tracing), Aditya (security/compliance questions), Marissa (POC coordination).
- FintechX: Product owner for POC (please confirm name), SRE/infra contact for log retrieval and storage.

Next steps:
1) FintechX confirms success criteria and POC kickoff date (proposed: Tue Mar 30, 10:00 AM PT).
2) Redwood shares dashboard mockups and MAP (attached).
3) Kickoff + environment access and sample workload within 48 hours of kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Marcus to schedule a short observability deep-dive right after kickoff.

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick confirmations and a couple of additions from our side:

We confirm the proposed timeline and general success criteria. A few items we need included in the observability scope:
- Please include p99 latency (this is critical for payments).
- Token accounting: per-request token consumption and a simple daily aggregate so we can estimate costs.
- End-to-end latency (client -> Redwood -> model -> client) as well as model-internal inference time if possible.
- Trace sampling: we'd like traces at 10% by default, with the ability to increase to 100% for short windows.
- Structured log export: prefer S3 in our AWS account (we'll share bucket + IAM role). Retention: 90 days by default.

Security/compliance note: we'll need confirmation that no raw payment data is persisted in logs or longer-term storage — Aditya, can you confirm Greenwood's (Redwood's) logging policy for POC sandboxes?

Kickoff: Tue Mar 30 at 10:00 AM PT works for us — please send invite.

Thanks,
Sara Thompson
VP Product, FintechX

Hi all — looping in with a short plan from the engineering side on observability panels, tracing, and exports. I attached a one-page checklist that maps deliverables to owners.

Proposed dashboard panels (will provide Datadog + Grafana examples):
- Request rate (RPS) by route / endpoint (1m, 5m, 1h)
- Latency distributions (p50 / p95 / p99) end-to-end and model-only where instrumented
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and failed response types (timeout, model error)
- Token usage: tokens per request, tokens per minute, daily aggregate
- Cache metrics: prefix/KV cache hit rate, cache size, cache eviction events
- Resource metrics: GPU utilization, CPU, memory, queue depth, worker thread counts
- Cost proxy metric: tokens * model-rate to estimate spend in dashboards

Tracing / instrumenting:
- We'll provide OpenTelemetry instrumentation snippets for the client integration and a sample span design for the inference pipeline (ingest -> preproc -> inference -> postproc -> return).
- Default sampling at 10% with a quick toggle to 100% (we'll include runbook steps).

Logs / export:
- Structured JSON logs with request_id and trace_id. We can export to your S3 bucket via cross-account role; retention configurable (default: 90 days).

ALERTS & RUNBOOKS:
- Suggested alerts: p99 latency > 500ms sustained for 5m; error rate > 1% for 5m; cache hit rate < 80% drop.
- We'll deliver a short runbook for triage steps and recommended mitigations.

Timeline & next actions for Redwood:
1) By Mon Mar 23: share dashboard mockups + checklist (attached).
2) By Fri Mar 27: provide OpenTelemetry examples and S3 export steps.
3) Kickoff Mar 30: setup dashboards in the sandbox and validate sample traces.

I'll build the dashboards and share a recording of the mockups prior to kickoff.

Thanks — Marcus
